findings.claim: The mandatory validation block hardcodes the machine-specific absolute worktree path '/Volumes/Thiamat II/stech/detran-worktrees/rait-backend' in a repository-tracked document (lines 14, 22-23, 29, 39). The absolute path is genuinely required because `pnpm --filter ... exec` changes cwd to packages/senatran-adapter, and the block is copy-paste executable in this exclusive worktree, but the same committed instructions silently fail-closed with a misleading 'file absent' result in any other clone, CI runner, or future worktree path, conflating environment mismatch with contract absence.
findings.fix: Derive the absolute path portably at the repo root inside the same block, e.g. `FILE="$PWD/docs/framework/contracts/manual/rait-priority-intake.commands.openapi.json"` guarded by a `test -f package.json`-style repo-root assertion, and use `"$FILE"` in the test/CLI/heredoc steps, keeping the fail-closed semantics and requiring no tooling change.

findings.claim: The gate requires recording 'the exact path, SHA-256, commands, exit codes and positive counts', but the executable block contains no command that computes the SHA-256 of the JSON; hash recording is left as unassisted operator prose while every other required evidence item (existence, counts, exit codes) is produced by an executed command, creating a gap where TASK-0029 and later gates could record a hash by hand incorrectly or omit it.
findings.fix: Append `shasum -a 256 "$FILE"` (or `openssl dgst -sha256 "$FILE"`) as an explicit final step of the fenced block, before `pnpm contracts:check`, so the recorded SHA comes from an executed command on the exact validated bytes.

findings.claim: The still-active 'Metas' section names future WP-C command contracts as root-level files (`BP-INF-RAIT-CASE-001.commands.openapi.json`, `BP-INF-RAIT-WORKLIST-001.commands.openapi.json`, etc.). Under the unchanged generated checker these root-level names would be rejected as orphans exactly like the rejected rait-priority-intake root path, and for the case module this naming is superseded by the decided `docs/framework/contracts/manual/rait-priority-intake.commands.openapi.json`. The delta's precedence notes (plan.md lines 21-29) quarantine only the rejected intake path, not this older goal text, leaving a latent repeat of the same reference-gap for future command contracts.
findings.fix: Add a short reconciliation note to plan.md (or the next authorized plan edit) stating that per the OWNER manual-OpenAPI decision all Architect-authored command contracts belong under docs/framework/contracts/manual/ with the manual README gate, and that the root-level `*.commands.openapi.json` names in Metas are historical naming, not writable targets.

Item 1 verified: the single operational path docs/framework/contracts/manual/rait-priority-intake.commands.openapi.json is genuinely outside the generated population without any tooling edit — tools/contracts/generate-openapi.mjs (frozen SHA 186b8036…, matching the reference-gap report) builds its expected set only from root `${bp.id}.openapi.json` names (lines 204-215) and its orphan scan uses non-recursive fs.readdirSync(outputDir) (lines 236-242), so the manual/ subdirectory is never scanned and the checker, its fail-closed orphan detection, and pnpm contracts:check remain byte-identical and mandatory. The rejected root path survives only as identified history: plan.md lines 21-24 explicitly mark it 'candidato histórico rejeitado, não uma instrução ativa'; C4-OD-V2-PROPOSED.md is declared non-dispatchable by the index; TASK-0029-V3-TOOLING-REFERENCE-GAP.md and the budget note record the gap as evidence; frozen review inputs are snapshots. No document reconstitutes a writable allowlist for the old path, and the TASK-0029 prompt forbids writing it (line 95).

Item 2 verified: the manual README block is installed, copy-paste executable and fail-closed in this worktree. `set -e` plus `test -s` rejects absent/empty files; the installed openapi-typescript 7.13.0 CLI (real devDependency of @detran/senatran-adapter, package.json line 40) performs parse/reference resolution with output discarded; the Redocly `struct`/`no-unresolved-refs` lint at error severity is resolved through the installed package via createRequire(import.meta.resolve('openapi-typescript'))('@redocly/openapi-core'), which is a real resolution chain (stdin-module base URL is the pnpm-filtered package cwd, where the openapi-typescript symlink and its .pnpm-linked @redocly/openapi-core dependency exist), exiting 1 on any problem; the surface script asserts OpenAPI 3.1.x, positive paths/operations, operationId, per-operation 2xx/2XX success responses and the exact intake POST /v1/inf/rait/cases, throwing (nonzero exit) on every violation and printing positive counts; `pnpm contracts:check` closes the block as a separate mandatory gate and the README states neither gate substitutes for the other. JSON.parse-only and CLI-only shortcuts are expressly ruled out (README lines 66-80; contract lines 1006-1015). The OD plan records a preflight demonstration of the mechanism on an existing contract with explicit non-transfer of that PASS to the future JSON. Feasibility rests on that recorded preflight plus static inspection; this reviewer did not execute the block.
